article_title: UCL and Imperial Researchers Find Chytrid-Fungus Survivor Toads Develop Antimicrobial Defenses While Still Tadpoles
summary: Submission approved with corrections: automated checks passed; sources fully verified; one subordinate misattribution (funding fact wrongly credited to Phys.org as well as ScienceDaily) requires a public corrections note.

findings.message: Source fetched via Archive.org fallback (original returned 200)
Funding fact attributed to two outlets, but only one supports it
findings.details: The body states: 'The work was funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and the Leverhulme Trust, according to ScienceDaily and Phys.org.' I grepped source-1.html.gz (Phys.org, read via its Archive.org snapshot per the manifest) for 'fund', 'NERC', and 'Leverhulme' — none appear anywhere in the article body (the only 'fund' hit was an unrelated JS variable 'fundingchoicesmessages'). The funding fact is accurate and does appear verbatim in source-0.html.gz (ScienceDaily, correctly cited) and independently in source-2.html.gz (Mirage News, not cited for this line). This is a subordinate body claim, not the headline/summary/lead, and the underlying fact holds — an honest corrections note covers it without needing to rewrite the article.

content_preview.title: UCL and Imperial Researchers Find Chytrid-Fungus Survivor Toads Develop Antimicrobial Defenses While Still Tadpoles
content_preview.summary: A Nature Chemical Biology study of Pyrenees toads finds fungus-outbreak survivors mature skin defenses earlier, as tadpoles, ahead of the disease's attack on adult skin.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Toads that survive outbreaks of one of the most destructive wildlife diseases on record mature their immune defenses earlier in life — while still tadpoles — according to a new study of common midwife toads in the Pyrenees published in Nature Chemical Biology. Researchers found that toads from recovering populations began secreting antimicrobial peptides from their skin before metamorphosis, according to [ScienceDaily](https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2026/07/260714225523.htm),...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (494 words, within the 400-1200 range for the category). Clear Overview / What We Know / What We Don't Know format. Neutral, non-sensational tone throughout; no AI self-reference; no editorializing. The 'What We Don't Know' section appropriately flags the unexplained fourth-lake outlier and the unanswered question of cross-species application, which is good editorial practice.
editor_notes.source_verification: All three source URLs were captured to disk by chief:review under sources/2026-07/ucl-and-imperial-researchers-find-chytrid-fungus-survivor-toads-develop-antimicrobial-defenses-while-still-tadpoles/; I read every snapshot directly from disk (gunzip + full text extraction) and did not re-WebFetch any live URL. Integrity check: gunzip'd each .html.gz and re-hashed with shasum -a 256; all three sha256 values matched manifest.json exactly (source-0: d3b5ae16a8ea27a6b13049159821b1824c7cfe9506ed187d27f6e14225298a06; source-1: 930dfec015d30055f6205bff949efd513cc49046923d8f63d0c1e5fb5ffc8c27; source-2: 6fe12c6fee656c86b0f4f15789e4dbd95d24382438d604217046749a4eb7fe34). (1) source-0.html.gz = ScienceDaily, live fetch HTTP 200 — confirmed: study led by UCL/ZSL/Imperial, lead author Dr. Phillip Jervis, senior author Prof. Alethea Tabor, four Pyrenees lakes in France/Spain, Bd fungus/keratin-skin mechanism, 1,152 peptides identified with only 7 previously known, tadpoles with more peptide diversity surviving better, both Jervis quotes verbatim ('The disease kills toads...helps these toads survive' and 'Our study shows species...it just depends on timing'), Tabor quote verbatim ('We discovered a far greater diversity of peptides than we expected'), co-author Dr. Kersti Karu named directly in body text, Gonçalo M. Rosa and Kieran A. Bates confirmed in the journal-reference citation line, and the NERC + Leverhulme Trust funding line present verbatim. (2) source-1.html.gz = Phys.org, captured via Archive.org fallback per manifest.json (archive_fallback: true; the finding note 'original returned 200' just means the live URL was also reachable but the script fell back to the Wayback capture — I read the archived snapshot as instructed, since that is the version committed to provenance) — same underlying UCL press release, syndicated by Phys.org (dateline 14 July 2026, byline Gaby Clark/Andrew Zinin). Confirmed: 'Ibón de Acherito' named as one of the recovering lakes verbatim, the 1,152/7 peptide figures, both Jervis quotes verbatim, and the Tabor quote verbatim. I specifically grepped source-1 for 'fund', 'NERC', and 'Leverhulme' — none appear anywhere in the snapshot (only unrelated hit: JS variable 'fundingchoicesmessages'), so Phys.org does NOT support the funding-source claim the article attributes to it. (3) source-2.html.gz = Mirage News, live fetch HTTP 200 — same underlying release; confirmed the four-lake/one-declining-three-recovered claim verbatim ('Around one lake, the toads were dying in large numbers and nearly extinct, but around the other three lakes the populations had recovered'), the 1,152/7 peptide figures, and the NERC/Leverhulme funding mention (present here too, though the article does not cite Mirage for that line).
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every specific number, name, and quote in the article traces to at least one of the three cited snapshots, with one exception: the sentence 'The work was funded by the UK's Natural Environment Research Council (NERC) and the Leverhulme Trust, according to ScienceDaily and Phys.org' cites Phys.org as a second source for the funding fact, but the Phys.org snapshot does not mention NERC, the Leverhulme Trust, or any funding information at all. The fact itself is true and independently verifiable — it appears verbatim in the correctly-cited ScienceDaily snapshot and independently in the Mirage News snapshot (not cited for this line, but confirming the fact is real and outlet-independent). This is a subordinate claim well below the headline/summary/lead, the underlying fact is accurate, and one of the two cited outlets does support it — a clear case for a corrections note rather than rejection. No other claim shows this kind of mismatch: all quotes are verbatim (not paraphrased-in-quotes), and no orphan source URLs appear in the body (all three cited URLs are in article.sources and vice versa).
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and professional. No sensationalism, no loaded language, no editorializing. Attribution phrasing ('according to X', 'per X', 'X told Y') is used consistently and correctly for nearly every claim.
editor_notes.originality: Searched src/content/articles/ for 'chytrid', 'Batrachochytrium', 'midwife toad', 'amphibian', 'frog', and 'toad' (case-insensitive, full archive). No prior article covers this study, this fungus, or this research group. One tangentially related hit (2026-07/13-frog-gut-bacterium-ewingella-americana-...) concerns an unrelated JAIST cancer-microbiome study and shares no sources, facts, or angle with this submission. A March 2026 biodiversity-threats piece discusses amphibian decline only in passing as part of a broader climate/land-use story, with no overlap in specifics. This is a genuinely new topic — no duplicate or near-duplicate coverage found.
concerns: The funding sentence in the body ('...according to ScienceDaily and Phys.org') misattributes Phys.org as a source for the NERC/Leverhulme Trust funding fact; the Phys.org snapshot does not contain this information. The fact is true and confirmed by ScienceDaily (correctly cited) and independently by Mirage News. Filing a corrections record rather than rejecting, per the 'wrong outlet cited for a real fact' guidance.
recommendations: Future submissions should double-check that every named outlet in a multi-source attribution actually contains the specific fact being attributed, not just a related fact elsewhere in the same article.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Substantively strong, well-sourced science News piece with a single, narrow, subordinate misattribution (an extra outlet incorrectly credited for an otherwise-accurate funding detail). Does not touch the headline, summary, or lead. Publishing with a corrections note is the honest path; all other claims, quotes, and specifics verified verbatim against the archived source snapshots.
